summary: ```# Quick Start Part Two: How to Make a Maid Costume - Maid Skirt ## Introduction In this section, we will focus on creating the skirt for the maid costume. The skirt is a crucial part of the overall design, and it requires careful planning and execution. ## Designing the Skirt Next is the most important part: making the skirt itself. When creating the skirt, we need to draw a skirt that is wider and longer than the inner skirt. ### Creating the Board After creating the board by overlapping, we now put the board separately in the 2D window. Press `Ctrl + D` to create a symmetrical board. After creating the board, select it in the 3D space and rotate it to the side of the virtual model. #### Why Not Use the Frame? We avoid using the frame here because the board is still too long. Even if we set the frame to the maximum, it will still have some contrast with the model. In this case, we can place the whole board on the side of the virtual model. ### Preparing for Simulation When we switch the picture to the physical surface, we can see that the model is in the 3D space. Remember to ensure that your skirt is facing outward. Positioning it to the side helps the board and belt merge together, preventing any issues with the board passing through the model when sewing. ### Sewing the Skirt After positioning, we will use the line sewing tool to merge the top of the board and the belt together. Next, create the sewing line between the front and the back of the button. After opening the simulation by pressing the control key, we wait for the skirt to be worn. ## Adjusting the Skirt Properties After wearing the skirt, it is customary to reduce the particle spacing and conflict thickness. After reducing the particle spacing, the increase in the number of faces in the grid may slow down the overall simulation speed. Therefore, it is beneficial to freeze other unrelated boards in the early stages. ### Manual Adjustments When opening the simulation, we can manually drag the board to ensure its wrinkles are evenly distributed. Additionally, we can narrow the whole board slightly to minimize the wrinkles at the waist. ## Modifying the Fabric When choosing the middle board, the dual center can activate the center point. After activating the center point, any adjustments to the size or rotation of the board will be based on this point, ensuring balanced adjustments. Currently, the fabric we are using for the women's pool group looks very good overall. The body appears soft, so we choose to use the fabric from the previous skirt version, copying the same fabric and dragging it onto the newly created women's pool group. We then increase the bending strength of this piece of fabric a little. ### Simulation and Adjustments After opening the simulation, we will see that the skirt is slightly open and has some support, preventing it from sticking to the skin like before. When modifying properties, remember the number of diagonal lines is often smaller than the direction of the gold sand and the tail sand. ## Finalizing the Skirt Design After adjustments, we select the outer layer of the board. Press the Shift key to select more. After selecting, press `Shift + Q` to hide, then activate the frozen board inside. Let's simulate by pressing `Shift + W` to display all clothing boards. ### Reducing Inner Layer Board Rate Once the simulation is stable, we will gradually reduce the rate of the inner layer board from 40 to 100. Note that when shrinking, we must do it gradually to avoid instability. ### Analyzing Layer Compression Select the outer layer board and hide them to see that the inner layer board is more compressed due to the additional outer layers. As we increase the bending strength of the inner layer board, it will gradually stretch the outer board. ### Enhancing Wrinkle Details To achieve a more detailed wrinkle effect, reduce the particle diameter to 8 and simulate again. If we want to make the skirt look softer, we can reduce the fine-tuning strength and the strength of the corner line slightly. This reduction will make the straightness of the entire board more apparent. ## Completing the Skirt To activate the belt, simulate it together and apply these modifications. All boards can be activated and simulated together. In my video, I made the top and skirt separately, but you could also sew the top directly to the belt for a unified design. ### Optimizing Details Let's optimize the details by selecting the flower edge of the middle part. Here, we can reduce the particle diameter of the flower edge slightly. At a particle diameter of 5, the folds will appear more delicate and the transitions smoother. ### Applying Pressure We need to use a tool called pressure. After selecting the board in the model editor, if we apply negative pressure to the board, it will receive a force from its front to its back, pressing the board against the virtual model. If the negative pressure seems too high, we can adjust the value to ensure a balance. ### Final Adjustments For the skirt, if pressure is insufficient at a value of 1, we can increase it. Higher pressure values lead to greater horizontal force applied to the board, enhancing its support. When modifying the inner skirt length, we must ensure that the boards do not overlap, as this will affect the UV mapping. Use the edit board tool to drag the bottom board of the skirt up to shorten it without conflicting with the outer board. ## Conclusion In summary, the skirt design process requires careful adjustments to properties such as particle diameter and pressure. By following these steps, we can create a well-structured and visually appealing maid skirt that complements the overall costume. ```
